raw_recipe.headline: Homemade Taco Seasoning Mix
raw_recipe.description: This mild taco seasoning blend is easy to make at home with the right spices, such as chili powder, paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, and cumin.

video.description: A simple taco seasoning mix that’s lower in salt than packaged mixes.

review.reviewBody: This made great beef taco filling. I used this for a pound of ground beef and used a little more than 3/4 of a cup of chicken broth and let it simmer until the liquid was gone, which was about 15 minutes on med-low. This wasn't spicy, but certainly not bland either and it didn't need anything to make it better. I did use the cayenne and crushed red pepper and used kosher salt instead of sea salt. Great recipe, thanks Kathy!

Giving it 4 stars because i haven't cooked with it yet. Just mixed it up and tasted it. Did one sub - used smokey paprika instead of regular - really gave it good flavor! I changed the servings to 50 so i could get a whole jar full to last me a month or two so used 1/4 tsp of cayenne pepper and 1/2 tsp of red pepper flakes since i wasn't sure how much a pinch was and wanted to keep it mild for my younger children. Can't wait to try it. So glad to find a recipe without cornstarch/flour/sugar!

Years ago, I was looking to make my own vs store bought and found this…so much better for us, physically and financially. And everyone loves when I make…family, parties, graduation! I do tweak it…I don’t have “hot” chili powder, just the regular from my cabinet. I don’t add the red pepper flakes, but do add one heavy shake (the “pinch”) of ground red pepper (vs cayenne). Biggest differences I think, however, are 1) I brown onion and minced garlic w/the meat (so I eliminate the powder versions in the dry mix) and 2) after draining the meat, then adding the dry mix to the meat mixture, I add about 50/50 water and salsa, abt 1/2 cup ea. It gives the extra flavor and texture I think some reviewers felt was missing!

A great base recipe. I'd add coriander seeds and celery powder (which I make in the dehydrator whenever I trim the leaves from celery stocks). Another tip: use whole spices when you can (peppercorns, cumin, coriander, dried peppers) and toast them on low heat in a sauce pan till fragrant, and then grind with the rest (except salt), adjusting with salt only at the end.

Loved it! Wanted tacos and didn't have any seasoning so AllRecipies to the rescue! Found this recipe lickety split and 30 minutes later we were feasting on absolutley delicious tacos! Yippee, this is now my go to seasoning. I didn't have any oregano so I subbed in Thyme and it worked great. Also, another reviewer said she used 3/4 chicken broth instead of water, so I did that too. I browned and drained one pound of ground beef, then added the seasoning, 3/4 cup of chicken broth and stirred until it came to a boil. Lowerd the heat to simmer for about 10 more minutes. Everyone loved them and went back for seconds and thirds! Bye bye little seasoning packets I have need of you no more!
Great! Convenient to have on hand to make smaller batches of taco or other "Mexican" filling, for 1 or 2. We like HOT and spicy, so I added 1/2 teaspoon of ghost pepper powder.

We didn’t have onion powder on hand, and the oregano was larger pieces, so blitzed everything in the spice grinder. I also subbed more paprika for the chili pepper amour and then added a dash of the chili instead. We have mostly mild spice eaters in the house. Instead adding the water I added tomato purée for more flavor. Didn’t miss the packet crap at all, thank you!

Big hit at my house, I keep some made up so everyone can use it whenever they want! I have changed out onion powder to minced dried onions and I put it on the raw meat and cook it with it, not adding water. Stronger flavor. The kids put it on quesadillas!

The recipe goes with one pound of ground beef. I used 93% lean ground beef. I used no cornstarch or flour. I added just over 1/2 cup of water, brought to a boil, then simmered until all the liquid cooked away. This recipe stands on its own, and it's nice knowing exactly what is going into my dish.
This is it. The perfect Tex-Mex taco seasoning. I skipped the pepper flakes and reduced the salt (because I had already seasoned the beef with salt), and it was exactly what we were looking for. :-)

So, I made tacos tonight and as I started browning the meat I realized I forgot to get a seasoning packet. So, I quickly looked online and found this recipe. It is so easy and flavourful. I put a bit more Paprika and a teaspoon less hot chili powder (and I used mild because Hubby doesn't like spicy) and a little more garlic powder. I'll be doing this from now on!
I loved this spice mix.
Best seasoning you can have. Better than any stir bought.
Been using this recipe for a few years. It's the only way i'll make Tacos now - much tastier than buying pre-made store bought Old Elpaso taco seasoning. thx!

It was fab and as a family we liked the flavour better than our regular taco seasoning. We had to leave out the onion powder as we didn't have any but added chopped onions to the minced beef instead. Was absolutely fine.
Added 1 tbsp of corn starch
I’ve been using it for years! Love it!
This did the trick quite nicely. Used regular chilly powder though, and doubled the recipe for one pound of beef. Wanted more flavour. 😉
I used 1tsp paprika and 1/2 tsp smoked paprika. That's the only thing I changed in the recipe.
Much better than store bought pkgs
